representation: verbatim recorded fields; inherited source review, not a fresh measurement

candidates.demonstrated_gap: The winner's release provenance was never verified (gpt6 records 'Artifact verification was not performed'), and the stack installs from PyPI. This lane identified the generator and the upstream's own verifier. At v2.0.0rc6, .github/workflows/build.yml runs 'Attest wheel provenance' through ./.github/actions/attest-build-provenance-retry, which cites https://github.com/actions/attest-build-provenance, with subject-path dist/nautilus_trader-*.whl. A 'Prepare wheel attestation siblings' step then builds the .whl.sigstore and .whl.intoto.jsonl assets from that step's bundle-path. 'Verify wheel attestations' runs scripts/ci/verify-gh-attestations.bash, which calls `gh attestation verify "$subject" --repo ... --cert-identity ... --cert-oidc-issuer ...`. The identity is ${server_url}/${workflow_ref} and the issuer is https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com. So the generator's supported verifier is the GitHub CLI's attestation verify, not slsa-github-generator tooling. Measured from primary sources: the release-asset digests equal the PyPI sha256 values in the decision record. rc5 is eab45fafd2312deda1236554c49a9798bfc76bc8465af864878e2f70189ebebe at 69,963,442 bytes; rc6 is 9b4002a7bf5e6399c51073039b740ccf3ca7a1e2584ff72c7d479f03eaa9658d at 69,828,675 bytes. The attestations API queried by the rc6 manylinux digest returns two Sigstore bundle v0.3 attestations, one user-initiated with a Rekor tlog entry and one GitHub-initiated. PyPI's integrity API for that exact file returns a PEP 740 attestation with publisher kind GitHub, repository nautechsystems/nautilus_trader, workflow build.yml, environment release. GHSA lists no pip advisories for nautilus_trader. An actual cryptographic verification run has not been done. cli/cli is maintained (commit 54a671d9a8f8c7a785c132d6f6a25375dc96acc1, 2026-10-12; v2.102.0).
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: On each host, take the exact rc5 and rc6 wheel files that uv.lock resolves: manylinux_2_34_x86_64 on Linux and macosx_11_0_arm64 on the Macs. Run `gh attestation verify <wheel> --repo nautechsystems/nautilus_trader --cert-identity <the identity the upstream verify script checks, server_url/workflow_ref, with the exact @refs suffix resolved at trial time> --cert-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com`. If the CLI accepts it, repeat offline with --bundle against the release's .intoto.jsonl sibling (untested). Pass means verification succeeds for that signer workflow and the verified digest equals the uv.lock sha256. A verification failure, a signer mismatch, or a lock digest that no attestation covers blocks that wheel and overturns the provenance assumption.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: The rc6 upgrade directly addresses weaknesses relevant to the retained rc5 destination: upstream reports corrections to reconciliation, fills arriving after expiry, simulated cancellations and Decimal conversion. Trial v2.0.0rc6 at commit 7b766f8825b2539c5b2ac1375e9d97b41c509edb. This evidence does not establish that the outstanding equity cash/dividend semantics or either broker acceptance gate now pass.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Compare rc5, pinned rc6 and the unchanged LEAN oracle on the frozen SPY inputs. Require all four previously failing parity checks to pass at their existing tolerances, no regressions in retained stress cases, and identical normalized ledgers over ten repeats. Then test ownership, partial fills, cancellation, duplicate events and reconnect reconciliation separately for IBKR and Alpaca. Start on Linux; published macOS arm64 wheels justify a separate native Mac qualification, not an assumed pass.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: next_action requires native in-flight failure and reconciliation to be qualified separately for IBKR and Alpaca. open_gaps[3] records 'Native in-flight broker fault behavior is also unqualified', and no fault-injection harness had been surveyed. The rc6 live docs state that 'A disconnect by itself does not reject, cancel, or resolve an in-flight command; stream updates, queries, or reconciliation provide that evidence'. Qualification therefore needs reproducible socket faults while commands are in flight. Toxiproxy describes itself as 'A TCP proxy to simulate network and system conditions for chaos and resiliency testing'. Its README documents a reset_peer toxic ('Simulate TCP RESET (Connection reset by peer) on the connections by closing the stub Input immediately or after a timeout') and latency toxics added with toxiproxy-cli (e.g. `toxic add -t latency -a latency=1000`). It is maintained: default-branch commit 94adfebb88bb6db251dea8aea4b23513e6aad084 (2026-10-08). The latest tag, v2.12.0 (2025-03-18), is old but sits on an active branch, so it is not stale. Using it for the IBKR leg rests on an operator design assumption, to confirm at trial time: the assumption is that the TWS/IB Gateway API session is a plain TCP socket that a TCP proxy can sit in front of. Alpaca HTTPS/WSS needs a TLS-aware proxy (see mitmproxy); no IBKR or Alpaca document was read for this. Precondition: an IBKR paper login and IB Gateway. runtime-target.json records local_broker_acceptance not_established, so the trial becomes feasible only once paper access is established under the paper-lane policy. macOS binaries are unverified.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: On IBKR paper with Nautilus (the rc5 pin and rc6), route the adapter's gateway connection through a toxiproxy listener and script four cases: reset_peer right after submit and before acknowledgement, latency above the adapter's acknowledgement timeout, a reset during a partial fill, then reconnect. Each case passes if reconciliation resolves every in-flight order to IB's own order and execution reports, with no duplicate submission, no orphaned or phantom position, and cash and positions matching the broker. Compare each case with a no-fault baseline. A case that cannot be produced at the TCP layer refutes the harness for that case. An adapter that resolves state without broker evidence fails the adapter.

candidates.demonstrated_gap: The winner needs verified artifact provenance, but the inspected Nautilus rc6 build workflow already identifies a GitHub build-provenance action wrapper, prepares per-wheel attestation siblings from its output and invokes scripts/ci/verify-gh-attestations.bash. No evidence established a need to add this separate verifier or its compatibility with those particular bundles. The decision is to follow and qualify Nautilus's supported verification path first; it is not a claim that slsa-verifier is generally incompatible or stale.
candidates.comparison_that_would_overturn: Reopen if inspection of the actual bundle predicate/builder identity and slsa-verifier's supported formats establishes a concrete advantage over the upstream verification path. A qualifying verification run must accept the published artifact and reject a changed wheel, wrong source repository/ref and unexpected signing identity. Separately require equality between the installed PyPI wheel SHA-256 and the corresponding release-asset digest. None of these cryptographic or byte-equality checks ran in this read-only round.
